Oh, I'm doing the Goodreads challenge as well. I'm a bit behind (9 books or so, hah).

I actually really disliked this challenge. The start and end of the list are okay, but a lot of them kind of suck to me. So many of the books are just based on the title. That's not a great way to choose to a book to me. You're not going to gain anything because you did or didn't read a book with a number in the title. You might as well just close your eyes and grab something it's so arbitrary. I feel the same about a lot of the "Read a book set in..." check, and I REALLY don't get the read a book with bad reviews. Why would you do that without anything else to go on. If you're trying to read more, the last thing I think you should do is pick up a book that's likely to be bad. Yeah, you may get a surprise, but probably not.

I love the idea of reading more, but this list looks more like clickbait crap than a decent list. It wouldn't be too hard to come up with a good list that would make you a better book conversationalist, or a "tasting" list dipping in to different genres or styles. You could flavor a checklist in all kinds of ways that would make it much more likely to serve as jumping off point to read more. I feel like I'd spend more time on this like trying to find a book with a number in the title that actually looked good, or one with antonyms, than I would actually reading the books.

So many of the books are just based on the title.

Well, yes. But I see this more as "okay, read a book with a number in the title, that actually interests you". Taking that same example, I kept postponing reading "Catch 22" for some reason, but when I got to that week I was like... "this is the perfect opportunity to do it".

I do get your point and I agree that this list could use some improvement. Why not make our own /v/books 2016 reading challenge? That would be interesting.
